root_cause.text: The GPIO reset controller is registered as a dynamically created auxiliary device without a devlink to its consumer, so exposing sysfs bind/unbind lets users detach it and free reset-control state that is still referenced, causing a use-after-free in `drivers/reset/reset-gpio.c`.
root_cause.evidence: The commit message says the device “is supposed to stay in memory forever” but “we also currently don't have a devlink between it and the actual reset consumer,” and warns that user-space unbinding “will cause a use-after-free splat from any user that puts the reset control handle”; the patch fixes this by setting `.suppress_bind_attrs = true` in the `reset_gpio_driver` to remove sysfs bind/unbind.

intent_record.intent_summary: Disable manual bind/unbind operations for the reset-gpio auxiliary driver.
intent_record.what: A new field assignment, `.suppress_bind_attrs = true,`, was added to the `.driver` initializer of `reset_gpio_driver`.
intent_record.how: This disables the driver bind/unbind sysfs attributes for the auxiliary driver, preventing users from manually binding or unbinding it at runtime.

grouping_result.intent: Disable manual bind/unbind operations for the reset-gpio auxiliary driver.

relevance_review.reason: The change directly addresses the reported root cause by disabling sysfs bind/unbind for the reset-gpio auxiliary driver, preventing users from detaching the device and triggering the use-after-free.

candidates.rationale: This defines the auxiliary driver's sysfs-visible driver identity that can be manually bound/unbound. Because the reset-gpio auxiliary device lacks a devlink to its consumer, allowing bind/unbind on this driver can detach it and free reset-control state still in use, leading to use-after-free.

Registering the reset-gpio driver as a module auxiliary driver exposes it to the auxiliary bus bind/unbind mechanism. In the vulnerable design, this makes manual unbind possible even though the device is still referenced, which can free state prematurely and trigger use-after-free.

vuln_statements.explanation: This defines the auxiliary driver's sysfs-visible identity, making it manually bindable/unbindable through the auxiliary bus. Because the reset-gpio auxiliary device had no devlink to its consumer, this exposed a path to detach the driver and free reset-control state still in use.

Registering the reset-gpio code as a module auxiliary driver exposes it to manual auxiliary bus bind/unbind operations. In the vulnerable design, that allowed users to unbind it while references still existed, leading to premature free and use-after-free.

bic_trace_step.reason: The shown function body is the initial implementation of the GPIO reset controller and does not contain any sysfs bind/unbind protection or devlink/consumer association. The relevant registration path is only: `return devm_reset_controller_register(dev, &priv->rc);` plus `platform_set_drvdata(pdev, &priv->rc);` and `priv->rc.dev = dev;`. The root cause described depends on the controller being “registered as a dynamically created auxiliary device without a devlink to its consumer,” which is not shown here; this code is a platform driver using devm-managed registration, not an auxiliary-device bind/unbind path. Therefore the vulnerable construct is absent in this snippet, and the fix is also not present because there is no mention of devlink or bind/unbind hardening.

Author: Bartosz Golaszewski <brgl@kernel.org>

    reset: gpio: convert the driver to using the auxiliary bus
    
    As the reset-gpio devices are purely virtual and never instantiated from
    real firmware nodes, let's convert the driver to using the - more
    fitting - auxiliary bus.
    
    Reviewed-by: Philipp Zabel <p.zabel@pengutronix.de>
    Acked-by: Linus Walleij <linus.walleij@linaro.org>
    Ac
bic_trace_step.reason: This snippet shows the driver converted away from the platform bus to the auxiliary bus: it changes `static int reset_gpio_probe(struct platform_device *pdev)` to `static int reset_gpio_probe(struct auxiliary_device *adev, ...)`, replaces `platform_set_drvdata(pdev, &priv->rc);` with `auxiliary_set_drvdata(adev, &priv->rc);`, and switches registration from `module_platform_driver(reset_gpio_driver);` to `module_auxiliary_driver(reset_gpio_driver);`. The vulnerable construct described in the root cause is the ability to detach a dynamically created auxiliary device via sysfs bind/unbind without proper linkage; in this commit version the code no longer uses the original platform-device path at all, so the specific vulnerable construct is absent here. The conversion to the auxiliary bus is the fix being introduced, so `is_fixed` is true.
